chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Old horns versus new: metal, workmanship and salesmanship
summary: He thinks old instruments sound better because of purer metal, comparing them to a hand-built Rolls Royce against a Ford.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Speaking of that sort of thing -- has the quality of instruments improved in the time -- during the time that you --

I think that the quality -- well into the workmanship, but the metal isn't as -- don't seem as nice and sturdy as it used to. I guess everybody is trying to save something. You know. But the metal of those old instruments -- that's why an old instrument sounds good -- that the metal is -- they've made it with purer things, you know. Good -- and the workmanship is good too. Of course they've had improvements and put things on assembly line sort of stuff now, you know. It's just like you get a Rolls Royce which is hand built and the Ford which has gone through the thing, you know. You've got something worth something when

you've got the Rolls Royce. And it's always going to be worth something. And that's the way with an old horn and a new horn. Especially if they ain't got smashed up or something, but still that metal is great and they used -- you know.
In this instance I'm thinking of the old metric old band pictures -- things have changed like the size of the bow and --
Well yeah, they've been improving things and they're doing things --
-- salesmanship a lot. A lot of it is for salesmanship. Like some trombones -- they used to put the slanty looking things on it to make it look streamlined and all that stuff.
Of course it wasn't no different than any other horn right on -- I mean -- the sound is what you got to think about. It isn't the looks of the thing. It's the sound that you get out of the horn.
And it seems like the old horns -- that the old metals seemed to be more -- I don't know what to say -- they sound better.
